glosses: To clean oneself by immersion in water or using water; to take a bath, have a bath.

examples.text: A Greek historian Phylarchus describes a white root indigenous to India that caused eunuchism when a person bathed in water in which the root was steeped.

glosses: To immerse oneself, or part of the body, in water for pleasure or refreshment; to swim.
To clean a person by immersion in water or using water; to give someone a bath.

examples.text: We bathe our baby before going to bed; other parents do it in the morning if they have time.

glosses: To apply water or other liquid to; to suffuse or cover with liquid.

examples.text: She bathed her eyes with liquid to remove the stinging chemical.
The nurse bathed his wound with a sponge.
The incoming tides bathed the coral reef.

All subtle thought, all curious fears,
⁠Borne down by gladness so complete,
⁠She bows, she bathes the Saviour’s feet
With costly spikenard and with tears.
Vorpal, eupeptically bubbling greetings, bathed a sausage in a swimming plate of sauce.

glosses: To cover or surround.

examples.text: The room was bathed in moonlight.
A dense fog bathed the city streets.

Although the encounter was bathed in sunshine, the match failed to reach boiling point but that will be of little concern to Gerard Houllier's team, who took a huge step forward before they face crucial matches against their relegation rivals.

glosses: To sunbathe.

examples.text: The women bathed in the sun.

glosses: The act of swimming or bathing, especially in the sea, a lake, or a river; a swimming bath.

examples.text: I'm going to have a midnight bathe tonight.

I do not feel disposed to ask any questions, but devote myself entirely to the Governoress, who takes me over to the bathing-house in her boat. I have had my bathe, and am strolling along the sands, waiting for the Countess.

glosses: To move through the water, without touching the bottom; to propel oneself in water by natural means.

examples.text: We were now all upon a Level, as to our travelling; being unshipp’d, for our Bark would swim no farther, and she was too heavy to carry on our Backs […]

He turned back to the scene before him and the enormous new block of council dwellings. The design was some way after Corbusier but the block was built up on plinths and resembled an Atlantic liner swimming diagonally across the site.

Meanwhile, NR faced an unexpected challenge when a night watchman spotted several Koi Carp swimming in floodwater close to the railway, after they had escaped from a nearby private residence. Wilson says the owner was eventually traced, and the fish were safely returned "after enjoying swimming around in a 3,000-acre lake".

glosses: To become immersed in, or as if in, or flooded with, or as if with, a liquid

examples.text: swimming in self-pity

glosses: To move around freely because of excess space.

examples.text: A fam'd Sur-tout he wears, which once was blue, / And his foot swims in a capacious shoe.

glosses: To traverse (a specific body of water, or a specific distance) by swimming; or, to use a specific swimming stroke; or, to compete in a specific swimming event.

examples.text: For exercise, we like to swim laps around the pool.
I want to swim the 200-yard breaststroke in the finals.
Sometimes he thought to swim the stormy main.

glosses: To cause to swim.

examples.text: to swim a horse across a river
Half of the guinea pigs were swum daily.

glosses: To float.

examples.text: sink or swim

Why, now, blow wind, swell billow, and swim bark!
The storm is up and all is on the hazard.
And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did swim.

glosses: To be overflowed or drenched.

examples.text: I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.
Sudden, the ditches ſwell; the meadows ſwim.

glosses: To immerse in water to make the lighter parts float.

examples.text: to swim wheat in order to select seed

glosses: To test (a suspected witch) by throwing into a river; those who floated rather than sinking were deemed to be witches.
To glide along with a waving motion.
To have a great quantity of something.

examples.text: You should be swimming in money after this job.

glosses: An act or instance of swimming.

examples.text: I'm going for a swim.

glosses: The sound, or air bladder, of a fish.
A part of a stream much frequented by fish.
A dance or dance move of the 1960s in which the arms are moved in imitation of various swimming strokes, such as freestyle, breaststroke, etc.

examples.text:

glosses: The flow of events; being in the swim of things.

examples.text: With the road ahead now clear, Mann […] is plunging back into the swim of business in a hurry.

glosses: A dizziness; swoon.
To be dizzy or vertiginous; have a giddy sensation; to have, or appear to have, a whirling motion.

examples.text: My head was swimming after drinking two bottles of cheap wine.

She snatched the letter from Sir Jasper, who started as her icy hand touched his: she attempted to read the passage herself, but the letters seemed to swim before her gaze: they turned to fire; the paper dropped from her grasp; a thick mist appeared to gather over the room; she gave a convulsive shudder, and dropped on the floor perfectly insensible.
